sections.html:
Newberg lies along the Willamette in Yamhill County, a drive of roughly 25 miles from Portland down Route 99W, and is counted in the Portland metro area. George Fox University stands in the heart of the city, so student renters live in many of the streets around downtown.

The city had 25,138 people in 2020, and the latest estimate, dated July 1, 2025, is 26,896. Only McMinnville is larger in the county.

An owner-occupied home in Newberg has a median value of $472,100. Treat that as a citywide midpoint and not a price for your address. Recent sales of similar houses close to yours will tell you far more.

sections.h2: Wet winters and what inspectors find
sections.html: Cool, soggy winters are the norm here: 39.95 inches of rain spread over about 152 days, plus roughly 33 freezing nights. Older Newberg houses tend to show the same weak points. Look for standing water in the crawl space, gutters that spill over the edge, and exposed pipes in unheated corners. Clearing the gutters and checking under the floor before you list costs little and keeps those items off the inspection report.

For years a single road, Route 99W, carried every commuter and delivery truck between Portland, Dundee and McMinnville, and traffic through town backed up badly. The Newberg-Dundee Bypass was designed to fix that. Its first phase, a four-mile road with one lane each way from OR 219 to OR 99W south of Dundee, opened January 6, 2018. The finished version would be an 11-mile four-lane expressway, yet money so far covers only Phase 1 and the design of Phase 2.

Buyers who drive to Portland care about this, so put commute time and highway access in your listing.

sections.h2: How Yamhill County sets taxable value
sections.html: Taxable value comes from ORS 308.146: it is whichever is smaller, the market value or a maximum assessed value that normally climbs by no more than 3% a year. The cap restarts when a property is new, rebuilt or substantially altered. If you added a room or divided a lot, your assessment may not track your neighbor's.

Yamhill County sends one bill and accepts it in three parts, due November 15, February 15 and May 15. Pay all of it by November 15 and the discount is 3%, or 2% for two-thirds. Anything late grows by 1 1/3% each month. Before you accept an offer, find out whether an installment is outstanding. The title company will pay it from your proceeds and divide the current year at closing.

Estate and foreclosure sales follow a lighter set of rules. ORS 105.470 leaves court-appointed personal representatives, trustees and foreclosing financial institutions out of the seller disclosure requirement.

Anyone else selling a one-to-four-unit home owes a signed disclosure statement to each buyer who puts an offer in writing. That buyer gets five business days to back out after receiving it, unless a waiver was signed. For an estate, line up the court paperwork before you list so escrow does not stall on authority to sign.

Yamhill County leads Oregon in vineyard acreage, with more than 80 wineries and six American Viticultural Areas lying wholly or partly within it. A Newberg-area seller with acreage, or a parcel outside city limits, should ask the city and the county which land-use and tax rules apply before choosing a price, because the two sets of rules differ.

• A listing with an agent versus an as-is offer from a cash buyer.
  • What repairs on an older house would cost versus selling in its present state.
  • The closing date, the tax split and utility transfers.
  • Whether a tenant or student renter is living there.
  • Whether the property is inside city limits.

No two buyers offer the same terms. Ask for each in writing and line them up.

When nobody is borrowing, there is no loan appraisal and no underwriter to wait for. Here is the usual order in Newberg.

  1. Tell the buyer where the house is, what shape it is in and when you want to leave.
  2. Read the written offer closely for closing costs, as-is wording and the closing date.
  3. Open escrow with a title company, which searches for liens and tax debt.
  4. Sign at closing. The deed is recorded and the proceeds come to you.

The title company is neutral. It holds funds and papers until everything on both sides is in place, which is why a clean file moves faster than a messy one.

sections.h2: If you owe taxes on the house
sections.html: Unpaid taxes come off the sale price at closing, interest included. A payoff statement from the title company, requested at the start, shows what you would net. It is also worth phoning the county tax office before you say yes to an offer so you know exactly which installments are open.

• Photo ID with the same name as the deed.
  • The newest property tax statement.
  • Your lender and loan number, when a mortgage is being paid off.
  • Lease and deposit records for any tenant.
  • Keys, garage openers and paperwork on permits or earlier repairs.

Handling an estate? Bring the court papers that show who may sign.

sections.h2: Timing the sale around a student renter
sections.html: With a university in the city, some houses carry a lease that follows the school calendar. If that is your situation, read the end date first and talk to the tenant early. A buyer who is told up front that the lease runs to a given month will plan around it, while one who finds out late may walk away or ask for a lower price.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready before offers
sections.html:
Small jobs count more than big ones. Clear the gutters, check the crawl space for water, and tidy any room a buyer will walk through. If a bigger repair is looming, such as a worn roof, decide whether you would rather pay for it now or accept a lower offer from someone who will handle it. Cash buyers often take houses as they stand, which can save you the repair bills and the weeks of showings, though the price reflects that.

Whatever route you choose, write down what you know about the house. Past leaks, additions, permits and the age of major systems all belong on the disclosure form when one is required, and clear answers keep a deal from unraveling late.

faqs.q: What county is Newberg, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Yamhill County, within the Portland metro area. McMinnville is the county seat, and Newberg is the second largest city in the county.

faqs.q: How many people live in Newberg?
faqs.a: The July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,896, up from 25,138 in 2020.
A planned 11-mile expressway on OR 18 meant to ease congestion on OR 99W. Phase 1, a four-mile stretch, opened January 6, 2018.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Newberg house?
faqs.a: November 15, February 15 and May 15. Full payment by November 15 earns a 3% discount, and two-thirds paid by then earns 2%.

faqs.q: Do I need a disclosure statement if I sell an inherited house in Newberg?
faqs.a: Not when a court-appointed personal representative or trustee is the seller, since ORS 105.470 excludes those sales. Other sellers of one-to-four-unit homes generally must provide one.
